content.text: Repair Ky option merging. Nested user data (especially json fields named headers, hooks, searchParams or context) must remain ordinary data, rather than receiving root-option special handling. Class instances such as a dispatcher must retain identity when supplied through create, extend or request overrides. Preserve the existing semantics for real root headers/hooks/searchParams/context, arrays, plain objects and null-prototype objects. Investigate the public request and factory paths and verify the fix.

The public request methods, `create`, and both forms of `extend` all use the same merge utility. Its recursive merge currently applies root-only handling to nested fields and can flatten class instances when an override is merged. I’ll scope the special handling to root options and restrict recursive merging to arrays and plain objects, including null-prototype objects.

content.text:
Implemented the repair in `source/utils/merge.ts`.

- Root-only handling for `headers`, `hooks`, `searchParams`, and `context` no longer applies to nested user data.
- Recursive merging is limited to arrays and plain objects, including null-prototype objects, so class instances such as dispatchers retain identity.
- Existing root-option merge behavior remains intact.

Investigated the shared merge path used by requests, `create`, and `extend`.

Verification: all 3 visible tests passed. Only the production merge source file was modified.
